attributes.root_cause_analysis: The function's --ops multiset is DIFFERS (ours-only: +1 addi +1 lwz vs target), fully and exactly explained by ONE cluster at target offset 0x374 (T[221:225]) where ours re-derives `(f32)(lbl_80344520 + 30)` (lwz+lis+lfd+addi, 4 insns) instead of reusing an already-live integer. Traced backward: target computes `lbl_80344520 + 30` ONCE at 0x1f4-0x200 (source line 3769's first AND-term `currentX > (f32)(lbl_80344520 + 30)`) and keeps the raw integer result live in r0 for ~0x170 bytes (0x204-0x374) spanning three more unrelated AND-term evaluations (`lbl_8034451C-30`, `lbl_80344514+40`, `lbl_80344518-20`), reusing it bare (just `xoris r5,r0,32768`) at 0x374 for the else-if's structurally-identical first AND-term (line 3784 `oldX > (f32)(lbl_80344520 + 30)`) -- a genuine cross-branch integer CSE by MWCC's allocator. Ours does NOT keep r0 live: the exact divergence is at target offset 0x224, where target emits `addi r3,r3,-30` (reusing r3, the register that just loaded lbl_8034451C, as both source and destination -- a dead-LHS in-place update) while ours emits `addi r0,r3,-30` (writing the SECOND AND-term's result into r0, clobbering the FIRST term's still-needed value). Every instruction before 0x224 is opcode-and-operand identical between target and ours (verified via fnasm --diff), so this is the single, precise, first point of divergence -- not a diffuse whole-function effect.
